The initial goal is to show that reversing the list [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] produces [5, 4, 3, 2, 1].
Rewriting reverse_cons removes the head 1 from the list being reversed and appends it to the end.
Rewriting again peels off 2: only [3, 4, 5] is still reversed, with [2] and then [1] appended.
Peeling off 3 leaves [4, 5] to reverse, followed by [3] ++ [2] ++ [1].
Peeling off 4 leaves just [5] to reverse; the left side already reads 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
The last rewrite peels off 5, so the list still being reversed is empty.
The reverse of the empty list is the empty list, both sides are now the same list, and rfl closes the equality.
